title: Parallax Concept Registry
description: Tracks every framework, foreign term, named concept, historical analogy, and strategic entity introduced across Parallax episodes. Enables cross-episode callbacks, visual consistency, and compounding knowledge.

_status.description: Lifecycle marker. 'draft' = the introducing episode hasn't published yet; this concept is provisional and tooling that surfaces concepts to viewers should skip it. 'published' (or absent — the default) = canonical and safe to consume.

type.description: Concept category. framework = analytical tool (game theory, Bayesian). foreign-term = non-English term with cultural weight (卡脖子). named-concept = a coined or established term (bifurcation, small yard high fence). historical-analogy = a specific historical episode used as a lens. entity = a company, organization, or regime relevant across episodes. mental-model = a reusable reasoning pattern (steelmanning, base rates). prediction = a falsifiable forward-looking claim with a timeframe (Oracle direction).

definition.description: One-sentence definition as it would appear in a concept card. Written for the audience, not for internal reference.

insight.description: The key non-obvious takeaway — what makes this concept worth introducing. The 'Wait, What?' moment.

introduced.description: Where and how this concept was first introduced to the audience.

appearances.description: Subsequent episodes that reference, deepen, or callback this concept.

relatedConcepts.description: IDs of concepts that are intellectually connected. Used for suggesting cross-references in future scripts.

pillar.description: Which content pillar(s) this concept serves.

tags.description: Free-form tags for filtering (arc names, regions, disciplines).

callbackVisual.description: Suggested visual treatment when this concept is referenced in a later episode (not re-introduced). E.g., '2s KineticTypography flash with original accent color' or 'brief FrameworkDiagram callback with dimmed detail'.

prediction.description: Prediction-specific fields. Required when type = 'prediction', omit for other types.

claim.description: The falsifiable prediction in plain language. E.g., 'China will not achieve sub-7nm chip production at scale by Q4 2027.'

probability.description: Rough probability estimate at time of publication (0-1). E.g., 0.6 for 60%.

timeframe.description: When to check this prediction. ISO date or quarter (e.g., '2027-Q4', '2028-06-30').

falsification.description: What specific observable event would prove this prediction wrong.

whatWouldChangeMyMind.description: The strongest evidence against the thesis that generated this prediction.

status.description: Current status. open = not yet checkable. confirmed/falsified = resolved by evidence. partially-confirmed = directionally right but details differ. expired = timeframe passed without clear resolution. revised = probability updated in a later episode.

date.description: When the prediction was resolved (ISO date).

evidence.description: What evidence confirmed or falsified the prediction.

episode.description: Episode where the resolution was discussed (e.g., 'EP12' or a 'Was I Right?' special).

updatedProbability.description: Revised probability if the prediction was updated rather than resolved.

scenarioName.description: If this prediction is part of a named scenario, the scenario name (e.g., 'The Murano Scenario').

watchSignals.description: Specific observables the audience can track. E.g., 'ASML Q3 earnings — China revenue share', 'Kalshi contract on Taiwan strait conflict'.

cn.description: Chinese term (characters). Omit if not applicable.

pinyin.description: Pinyin romanization. Omit if not applicable.

short.description: Abbreviated form for UI labels or lower-thirds (e.g., 'P.D.' for Prisoner's Dilemma).

beat.description: Beat number where the concept is first introduced. Null when registered before its host episode is finalized (e.g. cross-episode frameworks).

timestamp.description: Approximate timestamp range (e.g., '3:00-3:30'). Null until the episode publishes.

template.description: Remotion template used for the introduction visual (e.g., 'KineticTypography', 'FrameworkDiagram'). Null when treatment is 'organic' (no dedicated visual).

treatment.description: cold-intro = dedicated visual moment to introduce. organic = woven into narration without a dedicated visual. callback = referencing a concept introduced in a prior episode.

accentColor.description: Hex color used for this concept's introduction (for visual consistency in callbacks). Null when treatment is 'organic' (no dedicated visual moment).

beat.description: Beat number where the concept appears. Null when the appearance isn't pinned to a specific beat (e.g. running motif).

role.description: callback = brief visual reference to prior intro. deepened = concept is explored further with new facets. central = concept is the main subject of this episode. passing = mentioned in narration without visual treatment.

template.description: Template used (if any visual treatment). Null when role is 'passing' or callback uses no dedicated template.

notes.description: What new angle or context this appearance adds.
